site.name: Livingston Mine
site.location: Sugarloaf Mountain / Sugar Loaf Mining District
overview: Livingston Mine is a documented historic gold-and-silver mine on Sugarloaf Mountain in Boulder County's Sugar Loaf Mining District.
Federal mineral reports identify it as one of the county's important early-twentieth-century producers, while historic Boulder photographs preserve views of the mine in the 1890s and early 1900s.

timeline.text: A surviving Boulder Historical Society photograph documents the Livingston Mine and its surface buildings on Sugarloaf Mountain.
The U.S. Geological Survey described the Livingston as one of Boulder County's important producers and noted that the mine was developed by shafts.

moreHistory: The U.S. Geological Survey placed the Livingston in the Sugar Loaf district between Four Mile Creek and Boulder Creek and grouped it with the district's important producing properties.

Historic photographs in the Carnegie Library for Local History preserve the Livingston Mine as a named Sugarloaf Mountain operation. Those images were retained as research evidence, but no image with sufficiently clear redistribution rights was identified for app packaging.

A USGS/GNIS-derived mapped mine point at approximately 40.0258195, -105.4130504 is used as the historic mine-level identification anchor without claiming that a surviving shaft collar has been field surveyed.
